findings.summary: The new structured logger can never reach journald in the running service. log_mutation() emits through logging.getLogger("katana_work_folder_mcp").info(...), but the repository contains no logging configuration at all — a search for basicConfig / dictConfig / setLevel / log_level across the whole worktree returns zero hits, and server.main() only calls configure() plus mcp.run(transport="streamable-http"). The app logger therefore has no level of its own and inherits root's default WARNING with no root handler, so every governed_mutation INFO record is discarded before formatting. fastmcp's own configure_logging touches only the "FastMCP" logger namespace and uvicorn's LOGGING_CONFIG declares no "root" entry, which is exactly why the spec's §1 baseline journal showed only uvicorn access lines. Spec §2.3 ("新增结构化 logger（import logging，journald 可见）") and frozen acceptance commands §4.2 and §4.3 (journalctl must hit a structured line with mutation_id + DirtyWorkTreeError on failure, and mutation_id/commit on success) cannot pass against the real service. The error-code half of EK-3 is correct, but the observability half — the stated north star 「事务失败可归因」 — is not delivered at runtime.

The two journald regression tests cannot detect the defect above, violating constitution Article V (test-reality parity) which the spec §6 claims is satisfied. Both tests call caplog.set_level(logging.INFO), which forcibly lowers the root logger level and attaches pytest's own capturing handler for the duration of the test; the assertions then pass regardless of whether the deployed process would ever emit the record. A regression that pins the delivered behavior needs to assert on the logging configuration the service actually installs (e.g. that main()/configure() raises the katana_work_folder_mcp logger to INFO with a stderr handler), not only that log_mutation formats the right string once someone else has configured logging.

The two new _server_mutation branches return str(exc) directly instead of routing the envelope through _public_payload/_redact_string, unlike the MutationBrokenError branch immediately below. DirtyWorkTreeError is raised with an absolute-path-bearing message in several kernel paths ("cannot verify governed repository cleanliness: {exc}" and "cannot enumerate ignored repository payload: {exc}" wrap subprocess/OSError text that embeds repo_root), so wf_create/wf_save/wf_resume/wf_append_progress/wf_reindex can now surface a physical repo path in a public envelope. That contradicts the module contract stated in the server docstring ("返回值不暴露物理路径"); the fs_* surface is safe only because each fs_ tool wraps its result in _public_payload.

Spec §2.3/§5.3 place the structured logger on the server.py surface, but the implementation puts log_mutation in the package __init__ and calls it from FSTools._run_mutation and WorkFolderStore._call_mutate. Wrapping the kernel.mutate call sites is arguably the better seam — it covers every governed mutation on both surfaces with one success line and one failure line — but it is a deviation from the frozen minimum delivery set and leaves _server_mutation itself silent for any failure raised before kernel.mutate is entered. Per spec §2.3 the deviation should be recorded in the rework note rather than left implicit.
